fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Nighttime HAWK conspicuity and pedestrian exposure is a substantive safety concern.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The cited quote directly supports driver confusion from competing night-time background elements.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: The finding is correctly framed as a safety concern under US FHWA final-design audit context.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Installing a reflective border around the HAWK signal is specific and actionable.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are identified as the exposed vulnerable road users and paired with the beacon conspicuity risk.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance timing for elderly pedestrians at HAWK crossings is a substantive VRU safety issue.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The cited verbatim quote directly supports the concern that clearance may be short for elderly pedestrians.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: The finding is framed as a safety concern rather than a compliance question under FHWA final-design RSA guidance.
justifications.recommendation_quality: It gives a specific, actionable mitigation: reprogramme clearance intervals at all six HAWK crossings using a reduced assumed walking speed.
justifications.vru_coverage: Elderly pedestrians are explicitly identified and addressed.
